[{"ok":true,"path":"packages/ts/README.md","sha256":"16b4f3468b1260617e54032228ca2992964643ad176d28040f968d355e1e3533","totalLines":384,"startLine":1,"endLine":80,"lines":[{"line":1,"text":"# @graphrefly/ts"},{"line":2,"text":""},{"line":3,"text":"GraphReFly is a synchronous reactive graph runtime for TypeScript. You compose"},{"line":4,"text":"nodes, push data through explicit messages, inspect the live graph, and keep"},{"line":5,"text":"async work at clear source/adapter/executor boundaries."},{"line":6,"text":""},{"line":7,"text":"```bash"},{"line":8,"text":"npm install @graphrefly/ts"},{"line":9,"text":"```"},{"line":10,"text":""},{"line":11,"text":"## Quick Start"},{"line":12,"text":""},{"line":13,"text":"```ts"},{"line":14,"text":"import { graph } from \"@graphrefly/ts\";"},{"line":15,"text":""},{"line":16,"text":"const g = graph({ name: \"example\" });"},{"line":17,"text":""},{"line":18,"text":"const count = g.state(0, { name: \"count\" });"},{"line":19,"text":"const doubled = g.derived([count], (n) => n * 2, { name: \"doubled\" });"},{"line":20,"text":""},{"line":21,"text":"doubled.subscribe((msg) => {"},{"line":22,"text":"  if (msg[0] === \"DATA\") console.log(\"doubled\", msg[1]);"},{"line":23,"text":"});"},{"line":24,"text":""},{"line":25,"text":"count.set(3);"},{"line":26,"text":"```"},{"line":27,"text":""},{"line":28,"text":"The graph can also describe itself:"},{"line":29,"text":""},{"line":30,"text":"```ts"},{"line":31,"text":"console.log(g.topology());"},{"line":32,"text":"console.log(g.describe());"},{"line":33,"text":"```"},{"line":34,"text":""},{"line":35,"text":"## Core Ideas"},{"line":36,"text":""},{"line":37,"text":"- `state` is the sanctioned external input boundary."},{"line":38,"text":"- `derived` computes from declared dependencies."},{"line":39,"text":"- `producer` and source factories create graph-visible input streams."},{"line":40,"text":"- `effect` performs side effects from graph-visible values."},{"line":41,"text":"- Operators are node factories, not a second runtime."},{"line":42,"text":"- `describe()`, `topology()`, `observe()`, and `profile()` are read-only"},{"line":43,"text":"  inspection surfaces."},{"line":44,"text":""},{"line":45,"text":"The wave core is synchronous. Promises, timers, fetches, subprocesses, workers,"},{"line":46,"text":"and remote bridges belong at source, adapter, executor, worker, or wire-bridge"},{"line":47,"text":"boundaries. Otherwise BFS records each newly seen id at `cur.depth + 1` and marks `truncated` when a frontier node at the depth limit still has neighbors (diagnostics.ts:238-252). Paths are sorted by code unit (diagnostics.ts:98-100, 253) and depths are emitted in sorted key order (diagnostics.ts:257).

Worked examples for edges A→B, B→A, B→C (downstream = reverse deps, so A→B means B is downstream of A):
- (start=A, maxDepth=1): B is reached at depth 1; B's neighbors A (already seen) and C are not expanded because B sits at the depth limit, so C is not reported and `truncated` is true. Result: paths ["B"], depths {B:1}, truncated true.
- (start=A, maxDepth=0): no expansion; A has an adjacent downstream node (B), so paths [], depths {}, truncated true.
- (start=missing, maxDepth=2): the start id is not in the snapshot index, so the helper returns the empty result with `truncated` false (diagnostics.ts:228-229). Result: paths [], depths {}, truncated false.

Truncation is not proof of unseen nodes: `truncated` only means the walk stopped at a still-expandable frontier (diagnostics.ts:27, 241-243). In a graph containing only A↔B, `reachable(snapshot, "A", "downstream", { maxDepth: 0, withDetail: true })` reports `truncated: true` because B is adjacent, yet B is the only other node and is already fully known; there is no additional unseen node. Reinterpreting the flag as evidence of more nodes would fabricate reachability the snapshot does not contain, so the flag must be preserved as a statement about the bounded walk, not about the graph.

Finally, this report is a static, read-only projection of one frozen snapshot: it re-derives reachability from the snapshot's recorded deps/edges (diagnostics.ts:130-156) and reads no live Nodes (diagnostics.ts:176). It therefore proves only what that snapshot records about dependency structure. It does not prove that any future computation will run, that values will propagate, or that any physical effect will occur; those are runtime/lifecycle outcomes outside the snapshot's evidence.

lines.text: GraphReFly is a synchronous reactive graph runtime for TypeScript. You compose
nodes, push data through explicit messages, inspect the live graph, and keep
async work at clear source/adapter/executor boundaries.
The graph can also describe itself:
- `state` is the sanctioned external input boundary.
- `producer` and source factories create graph-visible input streams.
- `effect` performs side effects from graph-visible values.
- Operators are node factories, not a second runtime.
The wave core is synchronous. Promises, timers, fetches, subprocesses, workers,
and remote bridges belong at source, adapter, executor, worker, or wire-bridge
boundaries. Results re-enter the graph as facts, commands, or messages.
import { map, filter, scan, switchMap } from "@graphrefly/ts/operators";
The package also exports the common surface from the root:
import { graph, map, timer, memoryKv } from "@graphrefly/ts";
Start with the task you need to perform. These layers are not a required learning
sequence, and user experience levels do not select different runtime semantics.
| Compose an application and inspect its graph | `@graphrefly/ts/graph` or the root | Named nodes, explicit dependencies, composition and inspection |
| Implement a node or runtime integration | `@graphrefly/ts/core` | Low-level Node, Ctx, batch, protocol and dispatcher contracts |
| Represent business results and issues | `@graphrefly/ts/data` | Passive `DataResult<T>` and `DataIssue` payloads; no protocol ERROR or lifecycle behavior |
| Reuse a horizontal graph pattern | `@graphrefly/ts/patterns` | Existing patterns such as `admissionHandoff` and `eventFlow` |
| Use a domain solution | An existing focused `@graphrefly/ts/solutions/*` entry | The selected domain's inputs, policies and lifecycle contract |
| Connect existing values to a UI | `@graphrefly/ts/adapters` or a framework package | Observation and framework integration under the adapter's documented semantics |

You compose"},{"line":4,"text":"nodes, push data through explicit messages, inspect the live graph, and keep"},{"line":5,"text":"async work at clear source/adapter/executor boundaries."},{"line":6,"text":""},{"line":7,"text":"```bash"},{"line":8,"text":"npm install @graphrefly/ts"},{"line":9,"text":"```"},{"line":10,"text":""},{"line":11,"text":"## Quick Start"},{"line":12,"text":""},{"line":13,"text":"```ts"},{"line":14,"text":"import { graph } from \"@graphrefly/ts\";"},{"line":15,"text":""},{"line":16,"text":"const g = graph({ name: \"example\" });"},{"line":17,"text":""},{"line":18,"text":"const count = g.state(0, { name: \"count\" });"},{"line":19,"text":"const doubled = g.derived([count], (n) => n * 2, { name: \"doubled\" });"},{"line":20,"text":""},{"line":21,"text":"doubled.subscribe((msg) => {"},{"line":22,"text":"  if (msg[0] === \"DATA\") console.log(\"doubled\", msg[1]);"},{"line":23,"text":"});"},{"line":24,"text":""},{"line":25,"text":"count.set(3);"},{"line":26,"text":"```"},{"line":27,"text":""},{"line":28,"text":"The graph can also describe itself:"},{"line":29,"text":""},{"line":30,"text":"```ts"},{"line":31,"text":"console.log(g.topology());"},{"line":32,"text":"console.log(g.describe());"},{"line":33,"text":"```"},{"line":34,"text":""},{"line":35,"text":"## Core Ideas"},{"line":36,"text":""},{"line":37,"text":"- `state` is the sanctioned external input boundary."},{"line":38,"text":"- `derived` computes from declared dependencies."},{"line":39,"text":"- `producer` and source factories create graph-visible input streams."},{"line":40,"text":"- `effect` performs side effects from graph-visible values."},{"line":41,"text":"- Operators are node factories, not a second runtime."},{"line":42,"text":"- `describe()`, `topology()`, `observe()`, and `profile()` are read-only"},{"line":43,"text":"  inspection surfaces."},{"line":44,"text":""},{"line":45,"text":"The wave core is synchronous. You compose"},{"line":4,"text":"nodes, push data through explicit messages, inspect the live graph, and keep"},{"line":5,"text":"async work at clear source/adapter/executor boundaries."},{"line":6,"text":""},{"line":7,"text":"```bash"},{"line":8,"text":"npm install @graphrefly/ts"},{"line":9,"text":"```"},{"line":10,"text":""},{"line":11,"text":"## Quick Start"},{"line":12,"text":""},{"line":13,"text":"```ts"},{"line":14,"text":"import { graph } from \"@graphrefly/ts\";"},{"line":15,"text":""},{"line":16,"text":"const g = graph({ name: \"example\" });"},{"line":17,"text":""},{"line":18,"text":"const count = g.state(0, { name: \"count\" });"},{"line":19,"text":"const doubled = g.derived([count], (n) => n * 2, { name: \"doubled\" });"},{"line":20,"text":""},{"line":21,"text":"doubled.subscribe((msg) => {"},{"line":22,"text":"  if (msg[0] === \"DATA\") console.log(\"doubled\", msg[1]);"},{"line":23,"text":"});"},{"line":24,"text":""},{"line":25,"text":"count.set(3);"},{"line":26,"text":"```"},{"line":27,"text":""},{"line":28,"text":"The graph can also describe itself:"},{"line":29,"text":""},{"line":30,"text":"```ts"},{"line":31,"text":"console.log(g.topology());"},{"line":32,"text":"console.log(g.describe());"},{"line":33,"text":"```"},{"line":34,"text":""},{"line":35,"text":"## Core Ideas"},{"line":36,"text":""},{"line":37,"text":"- `state` is the sanctioned external input boundary."},{"line":38,"text":"- `derived` computes from declared dependencies."},{"line":39,"text":"- `producer` and source factories create graph-visible input streams."},{"line":40,"text":"- `effect` performs side effects from graph-visible values."},{"line":41,"text":"- Operators are node factories, not a second runtime."},{"line":42,"text":"- `describe()`, `topology()`, `observe()`, and `profile()` are read-only"},{"line":43,"text":"  inspection surfaces."},{"line":44,"text":""},{"line":45,"text":"The wave core is synchronous. Promises, timers, fetches, subprocesses, workers,"},{"line":46,"text":"and remote bridges belong at source, adapter, executor, worker, or wire-bridge"},{"line":47,"text":"boundaries. Results re-enter the graph as facts, commands, or messages."},{"line":48,"text":""},{"line":49,"text":"## Common Imports"},{"line":50,"text":""},{"line":51,"text":"```ts"},{"line":52,"text":"import { graph } from \"@graphrefly/ts/graph\";"},{"line":53,"text":"import { map, filter, scan, switchMap } from \"@graphrefly/ts/operators\";"},{"line":54,"text":"import { fromPromise, fromEvent, timer } from \"@graphrefly/ts/sources\";"},{"line":55,"text":"import { memoryKv } from \"@graphrefly/ts/storage\";"},{"line":56,"text":"import { describeToMermaid } from \"@graphrefly/ts/render\";"},{"line":57,"text":"import type { DataIssue, DataResult } from \"@graphrefly/ts/data\";"},{"line":58,"text":"```"},{"line":59,"text":""},{"line":60,"text":"The package also exports the common surface from the root:"},{"line":61,"text":""},{"line":62,"text":"```ts"},{"line":63,"text":"import { graph, map, timer, memoryKv } from \"@graphrefly/ts\";"},{"line":64,"text":"```"},{"line":65,"text":""},{"line":66,"text":"## Choose an entry by task"},{"line":67,"text":""},{"line":68,"text":"Start with the task you need to perform. [{"ok":true,"path":"packages/ts/README.md","sha256":"16b4f3468b1260617e54032228ca2992964643ad176d28040f968d355e1e3533","totalLines":384,"startLine":1,"endLine":80,"lines":[{"line":1,"text":"# @graphrefly/ts"},{"line":2,"text":""},{"line":3,"text":"GraphReFly is a synchronous reactive graph runtime for TypeScript. You compose"},{"line":4,"text":"nodes, push data through explicit messages, inspect the live graph, and keep"},{"line":5,"text":"async work at clear source/adapter/executor boundaries."},{"line":6,"text":""},{"line":7,"text":"```bash"},{"line":8,"text":"npm install @graphrefly/ts"},{"line":9,"text":"```"},{"line":10,"text":""},{"line":11,"text":"## Quick Start"},{"line":12,"text":""},{"line":13,"text":"```ts"},{"line":14,"text":"import { graph } from \"@graphrefly/ts\";"},{"line":15,"text":""},{"line":16,"text":"const g = graph({ name: \"example\" });"},{"line":17,"text":""},{"line":18,"text":"const count = g.state(0, { name: \"count\" });"},{"line":19,"text":"const doubled = g.derived([count], (n) => n * 2, { name: \"doubled\" });"},{"line":20,"text":""},{"line":21,"text":"doubled.subscribe((msg) => {"},{"line":22,"text":"  if (msg[0] === \"DATA\") console.log(\"doubled\", msg[1]);"},{"line":23,"text":"});"},{"line":24,"text":""},{"line":25,"text":"count.set(3);"},{"line":26,"text":"```"},{"line":27,"text":""},{"line":28,"text":"The graph can also describe itself:"},{"line":29,"text":""},{"line":30,"text":"```ts"},{"line":31,"text":"console.log(g.topology());"},{"line":32,"text":"console.log(g.describe());"},{"line":33,"text":"```"},{"line":34,"text":""},{"line":35,"text":"## Core Ideas"},{"line":36,"text":""},{"line":37,"text":"- `state` is the sanctioned external input boundary."},{"line":38,"text":"- `derived` computes from declared dependencies."},{"line":39,"text":"- `producer` and source factories create graph-visible input streams."},{"line":40,"text":"- `effect` performs side effects from graph-visible values."},{"line":41,"text":"- Operators are node factories, not a second runtime."},{"line":42,"text":"- `describe()`, `topology()`, `observe()`, and `profile()` are read-only"},{"line":43,"text":"  inspection surfaces."},{"line":44,"text":""},{"line":45,"text":"The wave core is synchronous. [{"ok":true,"path":"packages/ts/README.md","sha256":"16b4f3468b1260617e54032228ca2992964643ad176d28040f968d355e1e3533","totalLines":384,"startLine":1,"endLine":80,"lines":[{"line":1,"text":"# @graphrefly/ts"},{"line":2,"text":""},{"line":3,"text":"GraphReFly is a synchronous reactive graph runtime for TypeScript. You compose"},{"line":4,"text":"nodes, push data through explicit messages, inspect the live graph, and keep"},{"line":5,"text":"async work at clear source/adapter/executor boundaries."},{"line":6,"text":""},{"line":7,"text":"```bash"},{"line":8,"text":"npm install @graphrefly/ts"},{"line":9,"text":"```"},{"line":10,"text":""},{"line":11,"text":"## Quick Start"},{"line":12,"text":""},{"line":13,"text":"```ts"},{"line":14,"text":"import { graph } from \"@graphrefly/ts\";"},{"line":15,"text":""},{"line":16,"text":"const g = graph({ name: \"example\" });"},{"line":17,"text":""},{"line":18,"text":"const count = g.state(0, { name: \"count\" });"},{"line":19,"text":"const doubled = g.derived([count], (n) => n * 2, { name: \"doubled\" });"},{"line":20,"text":""},{"line":21,"text":"doubled.subscribe((msg) => {"},{"line":22,"text":"  if (msg[0] === \"DATA\") console.log(\"doubled\", msg[1]);"},{"line":23,"text":"});"},{"line":24,"text":""},{"line":25,"text":"count.set(3);"},{"line":26,"text":"```"},{"line":27,"text":""},{"line":28,"text":"The graph can also describe itself:"},{"line":29,"text":""},{"line":30,"text":"```ts"},{"line":31,"text":"console.log(g.topology());"},{"line":32,"text":"console.log(g.describe());"},{"line":33,"text":"```"},{"line":34,"text":""},{"line":35,"text":"## Core Ideas"},{"line":36,"text":""},{"line":37,"text":"- `state` is the sanctioned external input boundary."},{"line":38,"text":"- `derived` computes from declared dependencies."},{"line":39,"text":"- `producer` and source factories create graph-visible input streams."},{"line":40,"text":"- `effect` performs side effects from graph-visible values."},{"line":41,"text":"- Operators are node factories, not a second runtime."},{"line":42,"text":"- `describe()`, `topology()`, `observe()`, and `profile()` are read-only"},{"line":43,"text":"  inspection surfaces."},{"line":44,"text":""},{"line":45,"text":"The wave core is synchronous. [{"ok":true,"path":"packages/ts/README.md","sha256":"16b4f3468b1260617e54032228ca2992964643ad176d28040f968d355e1e3533","totalLines":384,"startLine":1,"endLine":80,"lines":[{"line":1,"text":"# @graphrefly/ts"},{"line":2,"text":""},{"line":3,"text":"GraphReFly is a synchronous reactive graph runtime for TypeScript. You compose"},{"line":4,"text":"nodes, push data through explicit messages, inspect the live graph, and keep"},{"line":5,"text":"async work at clear source/adapter/executor boundaries."},{"line":6,"text":""},{"line":7,"text":"```bash"},{"line":8,"text":"npm install @graphrefly/ts"},{"line":9,"text":"```"},{"line":10,"text":""},{"line":11,"text":"## Quick Start"},{"line":12,"text":""},{"line":13,"text":"```ts"},{"line":14,"text":"import { graph } from \"@graphrefly/ts\";"},{"line":15,"text":""},{"line":16,"text":"const g = graph({ name: \"example\" });"},{"line":17,"text":""},{"line":18,"text":"const count = g.state(0, { name: \"count\" });"},{"line":19,"text":"const doubled = g.derived([count], (n) => n * 2, { name: \"doubled\" });"},{"line":20,"text":""},{"line":21,"text":"doubled.subscribe((msg) => {"},{"line":22,"text":"  if (msg[0] === \"DATA\") console.log(\"doubled\", msg[1]);"},{"line":23,"text":"});"},{"line":24,"text":""},{"line":25,"text":"count.set(3);"},{"line":26,"text":"```"},{"line":27,"text":""},{"line":28,"text":"The graph can also describe itself:"},{"line":29,"text":""},{"line":30,"text":"```ts"},{"line":31,"text":"console.log(g.topology());"},{"line":32,"text":"console.log(g.describe());"},{"line":33,"text":"```"},{"line":34,"text":""},{"line":35,"text":"## Core Ideas"},{"line":36,"text":""},{"line":37,"text":"- `state` is the sanctioned external input boundary."},{"line":38,"text":"- `derived` computes from declared dependencies."},{"line":39,"text":"- `producer` and source factories create graph-visible input streams."},{"line":40,"text":"- `effect` performs side effects from graph-visible values."},{"line":41,"text":"- Operators are node factories, not a second runtime."},{"line":42,"text":"- `describe()`, `topology()`, `observe()`, and `profile()` are read-only"},{"line":43,"text":"  inspection surfaces."},{"line":44,"text":""},{"line":45,"text":"The wave core is synchronous. You compose"},{"line":4,"text":"nodes, push data through explicit messages, inspect the live graph, and keep"},{"line":5,"text":"async work at clear source/adapter/executor boundaries."},{"line":6,"text":""},{"line":7,"text":"```bash"},{"line":8,"text":"npm install @graphrefly/ts"},{"line":9,"text":"```"},{"line":10,"text":""},{"line":11,"text":"## Quick Start"},{"line":12,"text":""},{"line":13,"text":"```ts"},{"line":14,"text":"import { graph } from \"@graphrefly/ts\";"},{"line":15,"text":""},{"line":16,"text":"const g = graph({ name: \"example\" });"},{"line":17,"text":""},{"line":18,"text":"const count = g.state(0, { name: \"count\" });"},{"line":19,"text":"const doubled = g.derived([count], (n) => n * 2, { name: \"doubled\" });"},{"line":20,"text":""},{"line":21,"text":"doubled.subscribe((msg) => {"},{"line":22,"text":"  if (msg[0] === \"DATA\") console.log(\"doubled\", msg[1]);"},{"line":23,"text":"});"},{"line":24,"text":""},{"line":25,"text":"count.set(3);"},{"line":26,"text":"```"},{"line":27,"text":""},{"line":28,"text":"The graph can also describe itself:"},{"line":29,"text":""},{"line":30,"text":"```ts"},{"line":31,"text":"console.log(g.topology());"},{"line":32,"text":"console.log(g.describe());"},{"line":33,"text":"```"},{"line":34,"text":""},{"line":35,"text":"## Core Ideas"},{"line":36,"text":""},{"line":37,"text":"- `state` is the sanctioned external input boundary."},{"line":38,"text":"- `derived` computes from declared dependencies."},{"line":39,"text":"- `producer` and source factories create graph-visible input streams."},{"line":40,"text":"- `effect` performs side effects from graph-visible values."},{"line":41,"text":"- Operators are node factories, not a second runtime."},{"line":42,"text":"- `describe()`, `topology()`, `observe()`, and `profile()` are read-only"},{"line":43,"text":"  inspection surfaces."},{"line":44,"text":""},{"line":45,"text":"The wave core is synchronous. Promises, timers, fetches, subprocesses, workers,"},{"line":46,"text":"and remote bridges belong at source, adapter, executor, worker, or wire-bridge"},{"line":47,"text":"boundaries. Results re-enter the graph as facts, commands, or messages."},{"line":48,"text":""},{"line":49,"text":"## Common Imports"},{"line":50,"text":""},{"line":51,"text":"```ts"},{"line":52,"text":"import { graph } from \"@graphrefly/ts/graph\";"},{"line":53,"text":"import { map, filter, scan, switchMap } from \"@graphrefly/ts/operators\";"},{"line":54,"text":"import { fromPromise, fromEvent, timer } from \"@graphrefly/ts/sources\";"},{"line":55,"text":"import { memoryKv } from \"@graphrefly/ts/storage\";"},{"line":56,"text":"import { describeToMermaid } from \"@graphrefly/ts/render\";"},{"line":57,"text":"import type { DataIssue, DataResult } from \"@graphrefly/ts/data\";"},{"line":58,"text":"```"},{"line":59,"text":""},{"line":60,"text":"The package also exports the common surface from the root:"},{"line":61,"text":""},{"line":62,"text":"```ts"},{"line":63,"text":"import { graph, map, timer, memoryKv } from \"@graphrefly/ts\";"},{"line":64,"text":"```"},{"line":65,"text":""},{"line":66,"text":"## Choose an entry by task"},{"line":67,"text":""},{"line":68,"text":"Start with the task you need to perform.
